title: Joe Morello - Wikipedia
notes: Joseph Albert Morello, born 17 July 1928, Springfield, Massachusetts; died 12 March 2011, Irvington, New Jersey. Partially sighted from birth, blind from 1976. Violin from six, a soloist with the Boston Symphony at about nine; turned to the drums at 15 after hearing Heifetz. Teachers Joe Sefcik, George Lawrence Stone (who dedicated Accents & Rebounds to him) and Billy Gladstone. In New York with Johnny Smith, Tal Farlow, Stan Kenton, Phil Woods, Sal Salvador, Marian McPartland's trio, Jay McShann, Art Pepper, Howard McGhee; turned down Benny Goodman and Tommy Dorsey. The Dave Brubeck Quartet from 1955-56 to 1967 (the infobox has 1957-1972), more than 60 Brubeck albums. Time Out (1959): Take Five, written by Desmond to showcase his 5/4 playing; Blue Rondo à la Turk. Unsquare Dance 'solo in 7/4 with only sticks', Strange Meadow Lark, Pick-Up Sticks, Castilian Drums. Students: Danny Gottlieb, Max Weinberg, Jon Fishman, Tico Torres, Gerry Polci. Books: New Directions in Rhythm (1963), Off the Record (1966), Rudimental Jazz (1967), Master Studies (1983), Master Studies II (2006). Playboy poll seven years running, Down Beat five; Modern Drummer Hall of Fame 1988, Percussive Arts Society Hall of Fame 1993.

title: Scott Kevin Fish, "Joe Morello", Modern Drummer, March/April 1979, pp. 24-27, 50-51
notes: Read from the archive.org text of the issue. With Brubeck 'in 1955 until 1968'. Teachers: Joe Sefcick, 'a vaudeville drummer ... he played a lot of snare'; Lawrence Stone ('I went through Stick Control with Stone and I teach it ... the first part of the follow up book, Accents and Rebounds reflects some of my ideas'); Billy Gladstone, 'the greatest technician that I've ever seen ... everything was loose'. Influences: Davey Tough ('straight ahead on the big cymbal, but he got it cookin''), Sidney Catlett, J.C. Heard, Jo Jones ('Jo taught me a lot ... The only way you could play it was by pressing the beater into the head ... I learned a lot about hi-hats from Jo. He would really get a breathing sound'), Roy Haynes ('one of the most original drummers'), Buddy Rich's Quiet Please ('Buddy was responsible for my wanting to play'). On playing: 'I never used half of the technique that I have'; 'That's all technique is; the ability to play what's on your mind'; 'I like melodic playing which doesn't mean you have to have a million tom-toms. I still use the old four-piece drum set ... I like thematic playing. Theme development'; 'My whole thing is simplicity'; 'a drummer should never follow anyone. A drummer should lead'; drummers should 'know the structure of tunes'; brushes never practised, learned from listening to Jo Jones; 'I can't keep a single stroke roll for ten minutes like I used to'. On the drum battles: 'it makes a contest out of playing the drums. It lacks musicality.' Fronting his own quintet in New Jersey with his guide dog, Matthew.

title: Ludwig Super Classic Silver Sparkle Kit, Modern Drummer (30 September 2022)
notes: Morello played Ludwig where most of his jazz contemporaries played Gretsch: a four-piece Super Classic in silver sparkle, 14x22 bass drum, 9x13 tom, 16x16 floor toms; a 5x14 Black Beauty, Supraphonic or Super Sensitive snare. Quotes Andy Doerschuk (DRUM!, March 2011): 'a booming 14X22 bass drum'. Visible excerpt only (paywalled).

title: Time Out (Dave Brubeck Quartet album) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded 25 June, 1 July and 18 August 1959 at Columbia's 30th Street Studio, New York; released 14 December 1959; produced by Teo Macero. Brubeck, Desmond, Eugene Wright, Morello. Blue Rondo à la Turk 9/8 as 2+2+2+3, the solos in 4/4; Take Five in 5/4; Three to Get Ready, 3/4 then two bars of 3/4 and two of 4/4; Kathy's Waltz; Everybody's Jumpin' and Pick Up Sticks in 6/4. Desmond: 'It was never supposed to be a hit. It was supposed to be a Joe Morello drum solo.'

title: Take Five - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded 1 July 1959 (a first attempt on 25 June abandoned); written by Paul Desmond; E-flat minor; 176 beats a minute in the sheet music; a vamp on E-flat minor and B-flat minor seventh; the album version's drum solo, which the single cuts. Morello 'frequently soloed in 5/4'; the quartet closed concerts with it until 'only the drummer remained'. The first jazz single to sell a million; Grammy Hall of Fame 1996.

title: Blue Rondo à la Turk - Wikipedia
notes: Two sections: one in 9/8 'inspired by Turkish aksak rhythms', a four-bar cycle of three bars of 2+2+2+3 and one of 3+3+3, and one in 'a conventional swung 4/4'. Brubeck heard the rhythm from street musicians in Turkey: 'This rhythm is to us what the blues is to you.'

title: Joe Morello Tribute - Unsquare Dance - drum cover
notes: A cover on one snare: one stick laid across the rim and struck by the other, then strokes on the rim; 'a 1st class display of rudiments'. Its onsets run to under a tenth of a second apart at 211 to 236, faster than eighths.
